<USER_REQUEST>
Create a polished 10-slide investor/hackathon-style presentation for our project "Thervo", an AI-driven, sensor-free predictive cooling system for data centers.

The presentation is for the Yuva Yodha Tech Challenge under the "Smart Buildings" challenge. The goal is to present Thervo as a practical sustainability and energy-efficiency solution, not just an AI/ML research project.

IMPORTANT:
- Keep the presentation to exactly 10 slides.
- Use the project name "Thervo" consistently.
- Do NOT call it ThermaMind.
- Do not make the language sound AI-generated, overly corporate, or exaggerated.
- Keep text concise and presentation-friendly.
- Avoid paragraphs wherever possible.
- Use strong visual storytelling, diagrams, architecture graphics, data-center imagery, and clean infographics.
- Do not invent partnerships, customers, deployments, statistics, or results that are not provided.
- Do not claim guaranteed energy savings.
- Clearly distinguish current capabilities from future roadmap items.
- Make the presentation understandable to a non-technical jury while still showing strong technical depth.
- The overall story should be: Problem → Why it matters → Thervo → How it works → Why it is different → Impact → Execution → Team.

VISUAL STYLE:
- Modern deep-tech sustainability aesthetic.
- Dark, premium data-center-inspired visual theme with subtle green/cyan accents.
- Clean typography and generous whitespace.
- Use realistic data-center/server imagery sparingly.
- Prefer diagrams and visual explanations over decorative graphics.
- Make each slide visually distinct.
- Avoid excessive neon, generic AI robot imagery, stock-photo overload, and unnecessary icons.
- Use subtle animations/transitions if supported.
- Make charts and diagrams look like real engineering/product visuals.

SLIDE 1 — TITLE
Title: Thervo
Subtitle: Predictive Cooling for a More Efficient Digital World
Small supporting line:
"AI-driven, sensor-free thermal intelligence for data centers"

Visual:
A modern data center w
<truncated 5095 bytes>
- Baseline energy comparison

PHASE 2 — Production
- Multi-floor deployment
- DCIM integration
- API integration
- Access control

PHASE 3 — Intelligence Layer
- Temporal forecasting
- Anomaly detection
- Digital twin capabilities

PHASE 4 — Platform
- Multi-facility deployment
- SaaS offering
- Partner ecosystem

Clearly distinguish completed work from future development.

SLIDE 10 — TEAM + CLOSING
Title: Building a smarter way to cool the digital world

Introduce the team with clean profile placeholders:
- Name
- Role
- Technical/Business responsibility

Do not invent team members or roles. Leave editable placeholders if names are not provided.

Closing statement:
"Every computation creates heat. We believe cooling should be intelligent enough to know where that heat is going next."

Add:
Thervo
"Predict before you cool."

End with a clean visual of a data-center rack transitioning from high thermal risk to optimized targeted cooling.

FINAL DESIGN REQUIREMENTS:
- Keep all slide text concise.
- Use 1 strong message per slide.
- Use visual diagrams wherever possible.
- Use consistent terminology: workload telemetry, thermal risk, rack-level, predictive cooling, sensor-free.
- Do not overuse the words "AI", "revolutionary", "game-changing", or "cutting-edge".
- Make the presentation feel like a real product being built by an engineering team.
- The final deck should leave the jury understanding three things:
  1. Cooling waste is a real and growing problem.
  2. Thervo predicts thermal risk using information data centers already have.
  3. Thervo can make cooling more targeted, proactive, and sustainable.
</USER_REQUEST>

"import sys
import os
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE

def create_deck():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)
    blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]

    # Color Palette
    COLOR_BG = RGBColor(7, 9, 14)          # Dark #07090E
    COLOR_CARD = RGBColor(14, 18, 27)      # Card #0E121B
    COLOR_CYAN = RGBColor(0, 229, 255)     # Cyan #00E5FF
    COLOR_GREEN = RGBColor(0, 230, 118)    # Green #00E676
    COLOR_ORANGE = RGBColor(255, 145, 0)   # Orange #FF9100
    COLOR_RED = RGBColor(255, 61, 0)       # Red #FF3D00
    COLOR_TEXT_MAIN = RGBColor(240, 244, 248) # Crisp #F0F4F8
    COLOR_TEXT_MUTED = RGBColor(138, 153, 173) # Muted #8A99AD
    COLOR_BORDER = RGBColor(30, 38, 56)    # Border #1E2638

    def set_bg(slide):
        bg = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, 0, 0, Inches(13.333), Inches(7.5))
        bg.fill.solid()
        bg.fill.fore_color.rgb = COLOR_BG
        bg.line.fill.background()
        return bg

    def add_header(slide, tag_text, title_text, subtitle_text):
        # Tag
        tb_tag = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.4))
        tf_tag = tb_tag.text_frame
        tf_tag.word_wrap = True
        p_tag = tf_tag.paragraphs[0]
        p_tag.text = tag_text.upper()
        p_tag.font.size = Pt(11)
        p_tag.font.bold = True
        p_tag.font.name = "Arial"
        p_tag.font.color.rgb = COLOR_CYAN
